notes:
GIVER comes from the Campaign Header (NPC Name=Emhi Tchaoryo, Zone=Windurst Waters (S), pos=H-9); the walkthrough never names him, so step 1 is read from the header and cites bullet 2, the first walkthrough instruction, which presupposes the op has already been taken. Bullet 1 ('Solo mission') is a party-size remark, not a step. Bullet 2 sends you to the Quartermaster at (F-9): the page gives that grid but no zone, and Windurst Waters (S) is the only zone on the page, so steps 2-3 carry it -- a step left with no zone would silently inherit the giver's anyway, and here that inheritance happens to be what the page means. 'Quartermaster' is the name the wiki links ([[Quartermaster]]), not a description, but it is a generic name shared across the three nations, so it is only safe with the zone set -- flagged generic_npc_name. Bullet 3's thirteen supplies are ALTERNATIVES ('different players with different types of supplies'), so they are items_alt with their x-counts (Insect Wing x12, Gnat Wing x4, Treant Bulb x3, the other ten x1) and items stays empty: there is no item every player must hold. Holding one proves you are READY, not that you handed it over, so evidence is null on all three steps. THE PAGE STOPS AT THE LIST -- no bullet hands the items over and none returns to Emhi Tchaoryo, yet the header's Orders line reads 'Obtain shopping list from Quartermaster and submit items to her' and the Rewards block promises 680 Allied Notes that nothing in the walkthrough gives you. Step 3 is read from that Orders line. I did NOT add a return-to-giver rung: this page has none. The sibling page Stock and Awe II (S) does have one ('After you turn in your requested item to the Quartermaster ... speak with Rasdinice and you will receive your Allied Notes and completion of the mission'), which is why this record is medium and flagged walkthrough_incomplete rather than high -- but importing a step from another page is not reading this one. Separately, the Description calls her the 'republic quartermaster' when this is the Windurstian (Federation) op; the sibling Materiel Storm II (W) writes 'federation quartermaster'. Recorded as a page error; nothing in the ladder depends on it. Campaign Rank 'Allied Ribbon of Glory' is a real gate with no schema field and is NOT a character level (the Level field is empty) -- rank_gate_unmodelled. gates.repeatable and gates.expansion are null because {{Campaign Header}} has neither field and the page never states either in words.

notes: THE TIME LIMIT IS UNCONTRADICTED ON THIS PAGE, and that is what separates it from its siblings. notes: Two walkthrough bullets, read as three rungs. Bullet 1 is both the giver (Hieronymus, Bastok Markets (S), E-8 from the header, and named in the bullet) and the walk to the Quartermaster at Bastok Markets (S) (H-9) -- this page gives the zone AND the grid outright, which its Windurst sibling does not. Bullet 2 is the hand-over: 'Acquire the items requested by the Quartermaster and trade them two her for your reward' ('two' is the page's typo for 'to'). THE REWARD IS STATED TO COME FROM THE QUARTERMASTER, so the ladder ends there and I did not invent a walk back to Hieronymus -- but the family is inconsistent about this (Stock and Awe II (S) explicitly sends you back to its arbiter for the Allied Notes), and the Rewards block here promises 780 Allied Notes that bullet 2 does not obviously hand over, so this is flagged walkthrough_incomplete and the record is medium. THE ITEM LIST IS IN THE 'Notes' AFTER-SECTION, whose bullets restart at [1] and run to [18]; step 3 cites walkthrough bullet [2] and takes the list from there -- flagged steps_from_after_section. Those eighteen lines are ALTERNATIVES ('items requested by the Quartermaster', one player one request), so they are items_alt, never an AND-list. '6 Baked Apples' at [7] and '6 Baked Apple' at [13] are the same entry written twice, so seventeen are recorded. I used the canonical singular item names the wikilinks point at (Roast Mushroom, Grilled Hare, Stamina Apple, Dhalmel Steak, Baked Apple, and Honey for '8 Pots of Honey') rather than the page's plurals, because those are the names that resolve. Holding one proves readiness, not completion, so evidence is null. The Quartermaster is linked [[Quartermaster - Bastok Markets (S)|Quartermaster]]: the in-game name is 'Quartermaster' and the suffix is the wiki disambiguating between the three nations' quartermasters -- generic, so the zone is recorded with it. Campaign Rank 'Sterling Star' is unmodellable and is not gates.level; Level: Any and Time: None are no gates; repeatable/expansion null.

Structurally the same route as Crimson Domino I (B) -- and I read both rather than copying either, because they are NOT identical: the Rolanberry Fields (S) ??? is (G-10) 'near a small shed' here, carrying a {{verification}} tag in the wikitext and putting the page in Category:Verification, where Crimson Domino I (B) says (I-9) 'near a small open-air shed'. Each record keeps its own page's figure; flagged unverified_source_line. The rank and the rewards differ too (Sterling Star, 250 XP / 800 Allied Notes here against Brass Ribbon of Service, 150 / 600 on I (B)), which is the clearest sign these are two ops and not one page twice. Rendered bullets [3]-[6] are the gate sentries, [7]-[10] the ??? positions, [11]-[14] the campaign NPCs; the heading lines and the two closing sentences are unnumbered plain text rendered under the bullet above them, so step 14 cites [14]. The four Campaign NPCs are named on the page (Jagged Onyx, L.C.; Polished Fang, L.C.; Stray Boar, L.C.; Wayward Echo, L.C.) and those names -- not the 'List of Campaign NPCs' heading -- are the targets. Unit Requirement '1~6 members' has no schema field. Campaign Rank 'Sterling Star' is unmodellable and is NOT gates.level, which is empty on this page. repeatable/expansion null. The Gate Sentry is named by the page ([[Gate Sentry]]) and not by me, but it is a generic name worn by one NPC per campaign zone, so every one of those rungs carries its zone and grid -- without a zone the validator would demote the whole record, and a zoneless step would inherit the giver's city, which is nowhere near any of them. 'List of Gate Sentries:', 'List of ??? positions:' and 'List of Campaign NPCs:' are HEADINGS, not names, and none of them is used as a target. THE FOUR-WAY CHOICE IS AN OR, NOT A SET: you run whichever of the four areas your nation currently controls. The schema has no OR across steps, so each alternative is its own step in a shared group -- the group draws all four at once, which is the behaviour an OR wants even though the word means 'unordered set' -- flagged or_branch_modelled and unordered_group. The ??? group is marked optional because it only happens on the branch where the Gate Sentry did NOT hand the supplies over. EVIDENCE: the key item Campaign Supplies rides on the LAST ??? rung only. It can be obtained two ways (from the sentry directly or from a ???), rule 4 forbids the same item on two rungs, and putting it last means that holding it closes the sentry and ??? groups together and moves the mark to the delivery -- exactly where the player is. It is then handed over at the stronghold, so it is a consumed key item.
